nl_spans.text: At run time, CARA coordinates the Caregiver Interface, Blood Pressure Monitor, Algorithm, and Pump Monitors around an infusion pump that moves fluid into the patient, while sensor readings are stored in a shared buffer for software access.
nl_spans.rationale: Component list is mostly context, but shared-buffer sensor reading is an in-scope external-input obligation.

nl_spans.text: The pump has manual and autocontrol modes. In manual mode, pump speed is set with the built-in switch and the caregiver sets a default flow rate directly on the pump for manual operation, while in autocontrol mode pump speed is set by a control voltage from an external source.
nl_spans.rationale: Manual/autocontrol modes and control-source distinction are core mode-control semantics.

nl_spans.text: The Algorithm component controls infusion rate and records infusion-related data in log files; patient blood pressure is used to compute the infusion rate, with higher pressure producing a lower flow rate.
nl_spans.rationale: Flow-rate output, logging, and inverse BP-to-flow direction are modelable obligations.

nl_spans.text: The Caregiver Interface lets the caregiver modify target blood pressure and initiate or terminate algorithmic pump control, and it also displays and sounds error messages.
nl_spans.rationale: Setpoint modification, start/terminate events, and error-message outputs are discrete behavior obligations.

nl_spans.text: In the Mode_Control_Algorithm hierarchy, CARA has manual and autocontrol-related mode-control states plus an Ask_StartAC submode; within Ask_StartAC, the setpoint can be changed and pressing StartAC enters AutocontrolInit.
nl_spans.rationale: State names, Ask_StartAC, ChangeSetpoint, and StartAC transition are directly modelable.

nl_spans.text: During normal autocontrol, CARA controls flow rate only while there are no pump-operation complications.
nl_spans.rationale: Normal autocontrol and complication fallback constrain control ownership.

nl_spans.text: If a pump fault such as fluid-tubing occlusion occurs, the pump activates alarm signals, the caregiver removes the fault, and when CARA was controlling the pump the software releases control.
nl_spans.rationale: Fault, alarm, caregiver removal, and software control release are critical recovery obligations.

nl_spans.text: As a cross-component fallback, CA_backManual or any of CB_backManual, CP_backManual, or CC_backManual causes CA_mode to become Manual, making manual operation the shared recovery target.
nl_spans.rationale: Global back-to-manual events and Manual recovery target are critical fallback obligations.

score_rationales.FE: SD-2/SD-3 pass; SD-4 has no blocking diagnostics and all advisories have explicit output/abstraction waivers.
score_rationales.NGF: No critical/major contradiction; all in-scope required obligations are matched exactly or by declared abstraction.
score_rationales.REC: Weighted recall is approximately 0.932; no critical/major missing obligation.
score_rationales.GAS: Key guard/action direction is covered by BP_High/BP_Low scenarios, but continuous boundary and mutation probes are weak.
score_rationales.SCB: Full NL fragment is classified; limitations and abstractions are declared.
score_rationales.AAT: Major synthetic variables and output waivers are documented, but only self-reviewed.
score_rationales.BVS: Five default-prefix obligation-anchored scenarios pass SD-6 with no hot-start or model-derived oracle.
score_rationales.DMR: SD-5A reports broad mutation coverage gaps; only one wrong-target family is partially caught.

limitations: The model is a mode-control candidate, not a complete CARA system model.
Continuous blood pressure and infusion-rate computation are discretized into three integer levels.
Ask_StartAC is represented as an executable leaf state rather than a nested composite submode.
SD-5A mutation coverage remains weak; DMR=1.
NFRR is a single self-assessment with no independent adjudication or human signoff.
